title: IO Graph: Make LOAD graphs displayed
description:
After eb4e2cca69c5057995ff7d59848d784895904bb0 LOAD graphs aren't
displayed unless the fields element is incremented for items.
(This may not be the best way to do it, since LOAD graphs are guaranteed
to add non-negative elements, perhaps we don't want to treat them
like MIN, MAX, SUM, and AVG.)

Note that there's still an issue where graphs need to retap if
the Y-Axis changes, but that doesn't actually happen. (So, if
you start out with one of the other advanced types and then
switch to LOAD, it will use the wrong total time value, the one
for SUM instead of the LOAD version.)

Also use nstime_cmp in a couple nearby places for cleaner looking
code.

IO Graph: Make LOAD graphs displayed

After eb4e2cca69c5057995ff7d59848d784895904bb0 LOAD graphs aren't
displayed unless the fields element is incremented for items.
(This may not be the best way to do it, since LOAD graphs are guaranteed
to add non-negative elements, perhaps we don't want to treat them
like MIN, MAX, SUM, and AVG.)

Note that there's still an issue where graphs need to retap if
the Y-Axis changes, but that doesn't actually happen. (So, if
you start out with one of the other advanced types and then
switch to LOAD, it will use the wrong total time value, the one
for SUM instead of the LOAD version.)

Also use nstime_cmp in a couple nearby places for cleaner looking
code.
